_comment: The test-recording catalogue.  One entry per recording; tools/replaytest.py
runs them.  Add entries with `replaytest.py record <name> --description ...`,
remove them by deleting the entry and its .rec file.  See tests/README.md.
name         identifier used on the command line
saves        save fixture restored before the run, relative to the repo
level        level the recording plays, for humans
description  what the recording does and what it is good for
dt / seed    determinism settings; MUST match the recording's header
timeout      --auto-exit seconds; a safety net, the replay ends itself
expect.state fields from the KAROO_STATE_DUMP JSON that must match exactly;
omit a field to leave it unasserted
notes        anything a reader needs before trusting the entry

recordings.name: bombstart-crash
recordings.description: Hand-played by James, 2026-08-30. Navigates the main menu, loads save slot 4 (Forest\BombStart), plays about 10 seconds of the level — picks up one item and kills one foe — then quits. 1034 records over 1036 frames, 313 with a key held. The level is never completed; this exercises the menu, the save-slot load and the first seconds of gameplay, not a full run.
recordings.scenario: menu navigation + save-slot load + ~10s of BombStart gameplay
purpose: Stage D fixture: replaying it reproduces the recorded run's per-frame state checksum exactly.

Historically the deterministic reproducer for the CRASH.md guard-page fault — it crashed at frame 797 every time. That crash is now fixed (Game::RenderSceneObjects left textureCoords[1] uninitialised), so the recording runs to its own end and the entry guards against the crash coming back.
recordings.notes: Named for the crash it used to reproduce; kept under that name because tests/README.md and CRASH.md both reference it. Re-baselined 2026-08-31 after the crash fix: two consecutive runs produced byte-identical 1036-frame hash logs and identical end-state dumps.

recordings.name: bridge01
recordings.description: Loads slot 4 (Space\Bridge01) and crosses the bridges.
recordings.scenario: Loads slot 4 (Space\Bridge01) and crosses the bridges.
recordings.notes: Captured 1063 frames. No end-state assertions yet — run `replaytest.py --bless bridge01` once a replay is trusted.

recordings.name: castle-something
recordings.description: Hand-played by James, 2026-08-31. Navigates the main menu, loads save slot 4 (Castle\Something), collects 8 of the 41 items and quits about 11 seconds in without completing the level (8/40 gems, no foes killed, vitality down to 70 from damage taken). 1033 records over 1035 frames, 439 with a key held. Covers the menu, the save-slot load and the first seconds of Castle-theme gameplay; the level is never completed, so completed_a_level is false and there is no at_completion block. This is the only recording that exercises DrawQuadBatch's dwType==2 draw path (116 quads per frame) -- Forest\BombStart and Water\Water01 have no such object, so a change to karoo-hooks/quadbatch.cpp is only covered here.
recordings.scenario: Hand-played by James, 2026-08-31. Navigates the main menu, loads save slot 4 (Castle\Something), collects a few gems and then quits without completing the level. Covers the menu, the save-slot load and the first seconds of Castle-theme gameplay; the level is never completed, so there is no at_completion block. Captured to give the Castle theme's content coverage the Forest and Water recordings lack.
recordings.notes: Captured 1033 frames. No end-state assertions yet — run `replaytest.py --bless castle-something` once a replay is trusted.

recordings.name: destr-bait
recordings.description: Hand-played by James, isolated. Forest\DestrStart: does the bait manoeuvre and nothing else, then quits once the extra life at (11,3) is taken. The sequence is: climb the stairs, wait clear of the falling tiles so the foe commits to crossing the bridge, step on and off a tile to break it while he is mid-crossing, which severs his path and strands him on a falling cell so he drops; wait out the repeat fall (a tile a foe dies on re-arms from the stale occupant byte and falls again); then collect the life. Captured to measure the timings a tactical layer would need: how long the bait wait is, how many frames the foe takes to commit, and how long the repeat fall lasts.
recordings.scenario: bait the foe onto the falling bridge, break it under him, take the extra life
recordings.notes: Captured 2098 frames. No end-state assertions yet — run `replaytest.py --bless destr-bait` once a replay is trusted.

recordings.name: destr-extralife
recordings.description: Hand-played by James. Forest\DestrStart: collects the extra life (tile contents 7) at u=11,v=3, which sits in a pocket whose only approach is (10,4)->(11,4)->(11,3) with a foe spawning at (10,3). Captured to show how a human gets past that foe - whether it is dormant until triggered, and what the route and timing are - because the policy completes the level 30/30 but walks past this pickup.
recordings.scenario: extra life at (11,3), guarded by the foe at (10,3)
recordings.notes: Captured 4602 frames. No end-state assertions yet — run `replaytest.py --bless destr-extralife` once a replay is trusted.

recordings.name: gameover-forest
recordings.description:
Loads slot 4 (Forest\EnemyStart, one life), collects a few
                   crystals, then dies to the foe and runs out of lives, so
                   bGame_state hits 2 and DrawGameOverScore renders. Sits on
                   the game-over screen for a few seconds, then quits. The only
                   recording that reaches the game-over overlay.
recordings.notes: Captured 1491 frames, blessed on 18 fields. The ONLY recording that reaches the game-over overlay (bGame_state 2), so it is the only automated coverage of karoo-hooks/scoreoverlay.cpp Score_DrawGameOverScore -- the four capped "scoreoverlay: gameover" lines in karoo_hooks.log are how you check it still runs. One life, so the single death ends the game rather than respawning; lives=0 and death_cause=1 are the fields that say so. Scores are non-zero (4 gems, level_score 94) deliberately, so the breakdown draws real numbers in its count and product columns rather than a screen of zeros. The high-score half of that file is NOT covered here -- reach it with KAROO_MENU_NODE=3.

recordings.name: water01
recordings.description: Hand-played by James, 2026-08-31. Navigates the main menu, loads save slot 4 (Water\Water01), plays the level through to the exit collecting all 15 gems (15 of 15 items, no foes killed, no deaths), completes it at frame 3921 for a level score of 320, then launches into the following level and quits a few seconds in without saving. 4147 records over 4150 frames, 2102 with a key held.
recordings.scenario: full level run: menu, save-slot load, all 15 gems, exit reached, then into the next level
recordings.notes: Assert on the at_completion.* fields, not the top-level ones: the recording carries on into the next level, so the top-level block describes THAT level starting (gems 0/12, time_limit_s 220, level_complete 0), not Water01. at_completion latches the first completion and is Water01's. The score reproduces exactly from six fields: 75 gem base + 0 surplus + 0 foes + 92 time ((100-54)*2) + 75 all-items + 78 vitality = 320, and 1077 + 320 = 1397. Verified 2026-08-31: two consecutive runs gave byte-identical 4150-frame hash logs and identical end-state dumps.
purpose: The full-level counterpart to bombstart-crash, which never completes a level. Pins level completion and the score formula as regression guards.

Covers the score branch neither earlier run reached: the all-items bonus actually AWARDED (items_collected >= items_available with the +0x4220B flag clear). The two runs in REPLAY_PLAN.md both had it withheld.
Exercises a level transition, which no other recording does.
